title: Complex Seating Arrangements (7+ People)
tagline: Year 3 — Linear arrangements with seven or more people: anchors, chains, negative clues and case splitting

introduction.overview: A seating puzzle gives a set of conditions about who sits where and asks you to rebuild the unique arrangement. With seven or more people, guessing fails; you need a method. This chapter teaches the anchor-first method: start with the most definite clue, build chains of neighbours, handle "either-or" clues by splitting into two cases, and use negative clues only to eliminate.
introduction.placementRelevance: Seating puzzles with 7–10 people are a standard logical-reasoning section in company tests, and one puzzle often carries four or five questions.
introduction.realWorldContext: Allocating seats, shifts and desks under rules about who may sit near whom is the same kind of constraint problem.

learningObjectives: Build chains such as "X is immediately left of Y"
Split an either-or clue into two cases and kill one
Use negative clues only for elimination

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: When people face north, their left is the left side of the page. "Immediate" means adjacent; "second to the left" means one person between.

coreDefinitions: Anchor: a clue that fixes a seat exactly, such as "sits in the middle" or "sits at an end next to X".
Chain: several neighbour clues linked into a block of fixed relative order.
Case split: when a clue offers two options (either end), try each and discard the one that breaks another clue.
Positive clue: says where someone is. Negative clue: says where someone is not; use it last.
For people facing north, left of the page is their left; for people facing south it is reversed.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Every clue removes possibilities. Put the strongest clues in first so that later clues have only one place left to go.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Draw seven boxes. Fill the anchor, attach chains to it, split any either-or clue, and finish by elimination. Re-read every clue against the finished row.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Left/right count
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Right of seat s: n − s people

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Swap check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Re-write the row after the swap

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Verification
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Test every clue on the final row

mainNarrative: Take seven people P to V with the clues: P sits at an end; T is immediately left of P; V is in the middle; Q is immediately left of V; R is immediately right of V; U is immediately left of Q. Start with the two firm anchors: V is seat 4. Q is seat 3, R seat 5, and U seat 2. Since T is immediately left of P, P cannot be at the left end, so P is at the right end (seat 7), T seat 6 and S takes the remaining seat 1. The row is S, U, Q, V, R, T, P.

Always find the clue that has only one possible position. "Sits in the middle" gives one seat. "Sits at an end" gives two, so keep it for later. "Immediately left of Y" attaches X to Y and removes the left end for X's partner.

An either-or clue needs case splitting. In the clues "B and D sit at the two ends", "E sits next to B" and "C is immediately left of E", suppose B is at the left end. Then E is seat 2 and C would have to be seat 1, which is already B. So B is at the right end, E seat 6 and C seat 5.
Counting questions use the finished row. "How many people sit between L and O?" counts the seats strictly between them. "How many sit to the right of X" is 7 minus X's seat number.
What-if questions change the row, not the clues. Write the row, swap the two named people, and read the answer from the new row.

deepDiveAspects.title: Eliminating a case
deepDiveAspects.content: A case is dead the moment one clue is violated. Do not repair the case; discard it.

deepDiveAspects.title: Left vs right
deepDiveAspects.content: Left and right depend on the direction faced. Check the facing direction in the problem before you start.

problemVariations.exampleSnippet: B and D at the ends

solvedExamples.title: Anchors and chains
solvedExamples.question: Seven friends P to V sit in a row facing north. P sits at an end; T is immediately left of P; V is in the middle; Q is immediately left of V; R is immediately right of V; U is immediately left of Q. Who sits at the left end?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Anchor V, then attach the chains.

steps.title: Chain
steps.explanation: U, Q, V, R occupy seats 2, 3, 4, 5.

steps.title: Right end
steps.explanation: T is immediately left of P, so P is at the right end: T seat 6, P seat 7.

steps.title: Left end
steps.explanation: The only person left is S in seat 1.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The row is S, U, Q, V, R, T, P.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Placing P at the left end.

solvedExamples.title: Case split
solvedExamples.question: Seven colleagues A to G sit in a row facing north. G sits in the middle, A is immediately left of G, B and D sit at the two ends, E is next to B, C is immediately left of E, F is immediately right of D. Who sits at the right end?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Try B at the left end first.

steps.title: Case B at left
steps.explanation: E would be seat 2 and C seat 1, but seat 1 is B. Rejected.

steps.title: Case B at right
steps.explanation: E is seat 6 and C seat 5.

steps.title: Remaining
steps.explanation: G seat 4, A seat 3, D seat 1, F seat 2.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The row is D, F, A, G, C, E, B.

solvedExamples.title: What-if
solvedExamples.question: In the row S, U, Q, V, R, T, P, if U and T exchange seats, who sits immediately left of V?
givenInfo: Row S, U, Q, V, R, T, P

steps.title: Swap
steps.explanation: The new row is S, T, Q, V, R, U, P.

steps.title: Read
steps.explanation: Immediately left of V is Q.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The swap does not affect seat 3.

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Place people one by one in clue order.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Sort the clues by how few seats they allow, place those first, and split an either-or clue early.

commonMistakes.mistake: Counting seats instead of people between
Editing the original row in what-if questions

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: If an option contradicts any single clue, drop it at once.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: A clue that uses a name already placed is a free move.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The same puzzle carries several questions, so build the full row once.

quickFormulas: Right of seat s = n − s
